latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n > 1, and define f_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{j=1}^n floor(jx)/j.

Let k be an integer with 0 <= k < n, and let x,y be real numbers such that k/n <= x <= y < (k+1)/n. We must show that f_n(y) <= f_n(x).

Because y < (k+1)/n, we have ny < k+1, and since also ny >= k, it follows that floor(ny) = k. Similarly, nx >= k and nx < k+1, so floor(nx) = k. Thus on the whole interval [k/n, (k+1)/n), the term floor(nx) is constant and equal to k.

Now fix any j in {1,2,...,n}. Since x <= y, we have jx <= jy. The floor function is nondecreasing on the real line, so floor(jx) <= floor(jy). Dividing by the positive integer j preserves the inequality:

floor(jx)/j <= floor(jy)/j.

Summing these inequalities over j = 1,2,...,n gives

sum_{j=1}^n floor(jx)/j <= sum_{j=1}^n floor(jy)/j.

Using the constancy of floor(nx) and floor(ny), we obtain

f_n(x) = k - sum_{j=1}^n floor(jx)/j,

f_n(y) = k - sum_{j=1}^n floor(jy)/j.

Therefore

f_n(y) <= f_n(x).

Hence f_n is nonincreasing on the half-open interval [k/n, (k+1)/n), as claimed.
role_in_parent: Supplies the function-specific comparison on the grid cell containing m/n and r.
statement_nl: For every integer k with 0 <= k < n, the function f_n is nonincreasing on the half-open interval [k/n, (k + 1)/n): whenever x and y are real numbers with k/n <= x <= y < (k + 1)/n, one has f_n(y) <= f_n(x).

domain_restrictions: k satisfies 0 <= k and k < n
division is well-defined: n is not 0
x and y are real numbers
the monotonicity condition is only required when both x and y lie in the half-open interval [k/n, (k + 1)/n)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an index n (so f_n is fixed). For every integer k with 0 <= k < n, and for all real numbers x and y with k/n <= x <= y < (k + 1)/n, it holds that f_n(y) <= f_n(x).
